original_question: Problem 7.3 (S. Vũ Ngo.c). Write Bohr-Sommerfeld rules for focus-focus singularities in Berezin- Toeplitz quantisation.
target_in_paper: Section 7.1, Problem 7.3 (S. Vũ Ngọc): Write Bohr-Sommerfeld rules for focus-focus singularities in Berezin-Toeplitz quantisation. The surrounding paragraph says that these rules are sought in the Berezin-Toeplitz setting on compact Kähler manifolds, as an extension of known Toeplitz Bohr-Sommerfeld rules for regular tori and 1-dimensional Morse singularities, and along the lines of Vũ Ngọc’s focus-focus pseudodifferential analysis. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1804.03737))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper’s exact official open problem almost verbatim: it has the right operation (write Bohr-Sommerfeld rules), the right singularity type (focus-focus), the right quantisation scheme (Berezin-Toeplitz), and the right attribution/numbering target (Problem 7.3, S. Vũ Ngọc). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1804.03737))
missing_details: The draft does not state the ambient quantum setting used in §7.1: a quantum integrable system consists of commuting self-adjoint semiclassical operators whose principal symbols have almost-everywhere independent differentials. ([upcommons.upc.edu](https://upcommons.upc.edu/bitstreams/d858abf8-e232-45e3-a199-3adac6cf7893/download))

It does not say that, for the Berezin-Toeplitz version of the problem, the paper specifically has compact Kähler manifolds in mind (within the general prequantizable symplectic/Toeplitz framework introduced just above). ([upcommons.upc.edu](https://upcommons.upc.edu/bitstreams/d858abf8-e232-45e3-a199-3adac6cf7893/download))

It does not explain what the paper means by Bohr-Sommerfeld rules: all-order semiclassical integrality/cohomological conditions on E in R^n that hold if and only if E is a joint eigenvalue modulo O(h^∞) (or, in Toeplitz notation, modulo O(k^(-∞))). ([upcommons.upc.edu](https://upcommons.upc.edu/bitstreams/d858abf8-e232-45e3-a199-3adac6cf7893/download))

It does not make explicit that the sought rule is for the singular regime near a focus-focus critical value/fibre, as opposed to the already-treated regular torus case. ([upcommons.upc.edu](https://upcommons.upc.edu/bitstreams/d858abf8-e232-45e3-a199-3adac6cf7893/download))

It does not mention the intended model for the desired extension: the focus-focus Bohr-Sommerfeld theory for pseudodifferential operators cited by the paper as the line along which the Toeplitz case should be treated. ([upcommons.upc.edu](https://upcommons.upc.edu/bitstreams/d858abf8-e232-45e3-a199-3adac6cf7893/download))

It does not indicate the spectral purpose of the rule that becomes important in the next subsection: the singular Bohr-Sommerfeld rule is expected to control the spectrum at a focus-focus critical value and is tied to recovering the Taylor-series invariant/formal power series there. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1804.03737))
refined_question: Let (M, ω, J) be a compact prequantizable Kähler manifold with its Berezin-Toeplitz quantum spaces 𝓗_k and semiclassical parameter k^(-1), and let T_{1,k}, T_{2,k} be commuting self-adjoint Berezin-Toeplitz operators whose joint principal symbol F = (f_1, f_2) : M → R^2 defines a classical integrable system with a nondegenerate focus-focus singularity at a critical point m_0 and critical value c_0 = F(m_0). Formulate and prove an all-orders singular Bohr-Sommerfeld quantization rule that gives necessary and sufficient integrality/cohomological conditions for E_k near c_0 to lie in the joint spectrum of (T_{1,k}, T_{2,k}) modulo O(k^(-∞)), thereby extending the known Toeplitz Bohr-Sommerfeld rules for regular tori and for 1-degree-of-freedom Morse singularities to the focus-focus case, along the lines of Vũ Ngọc’s focus-focus pseudodifferential theory. ([upcommons.upc.edu](https://upcommons.upc.edu/bitstreams/d858abf8-e232-45e3-a199-3adac6cf7893/download))
justification: The draft is already very close because it reproduces the official one-line problem itself. The only substantive additions needed to make it stand-alone and paper-faithful are the ambient Toeplitz/quantum-integrable setting, the exact spectral meaning of Bohr-Sommerfeld rules supplied immediately above the problem, and the fact that the target is the singular joint-spectrum asymptotics near a focus-focus critical value. That last point is reinforced in §7.2, where the paper says that recovering the Taylor-series invariant directly from the spectrum at a focus-focus value should probably use the corresponding singular Bohr-Sommerfeld rule and then asks whether the associated formal power series is spectral. Page numbers in the citations array refer to the PDF pagination; section/problem numbering follows the final arXiv/PMC numbering. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1804.03737))
